name: Rococo court dress
summary: The court dress of Louis XV: a wide-hipped silk gown with Watteau back pleats, lace ruffles and flower brocade, copied at the courts of Europe.

philosophy.core_thesis: A court gown shows rank by the width of the skirt, the weight of the silk and the hours of hand work in the trim.
design_principles: Hold the skirt out on side hoops 1 m across for day and up to 3 m across for court.
Boned stays shape the torso into a stiff cone; lace the stays tight so that the back stays straight.
Cut the back as two box pleats that fall free from the neck to the floor (the Watteau pleat).
Open the front of the skirt over a petticoat in the same silk or a contrast silk.
Fill the V of the bodice with a stomacher, and cover it with bows or embroidery.
End the sleeve at the elbow in two or three tiers of lace ruffles.
Choose small flower sprays on a pale ground; keep the brocade pattern in scale with the skirt.
anti_patterns: A straight, narrow skirt with no hoops
Heavy, dark, plain wool for a court gown
A high neckline with no lace at the elbow
A waist at the natural line with no point at the front

silhouette.shape: A wide oval skirt on side hoops, over a tight, stiff, conical bodice with a point at the front.
silhouette.line: A low square neckline, a V-shaped stomacher and loose pleats that fall from the neck to the floor at the back.
silhouette.fit: Tight and boned at the torso, free at the back where the box pleats hang, and very wide at the hip.
silhouette.proportion: The waist is 55 to 65 cm. Day hoops are about 1 m across. Court hoops are up to 3 m across. The bodice ends in a point below the natural waist.
rules: Lace the stays from the back, and pull the bust up into a flat square neckline.
Tie the hoops at the waist so that the skirt is wide at the side and flat at the front and back.
Open the skirt at the front in an inverted V to show the petticoat.
Trim the edge of the skirt, the sleeve and the neckline with the same ruffle, bow or ruche.
Let the hem touch the floor for court and clear the ankle for day.

fabrics.rule: Choose a silk with body and a bright surface: brocade and satin for the gown, taffeta for the petticoat, velvet for the coat.

methods: side hoops of cane and whalebone
box pleats stitched at the back neck
lace sleeve ruffles sewn in tiers
trim ruched and gathered by hand
construction.closures: Pins at the front, hooks and laces at the back of the stays; the stomacher is pinned to the stays.
construction.details: Engageantes (lace cuffs) at the elbow, a ruched robings trim down the front, a choker ribbon and a small powdered coiffure to finish.

surface.pattern: Small flower sprays and ribbons woven into the silk on a pale ground; painted or printed chintz for the informal gown.
surface.gloss: Satin and taffeta at 40–70 GU; brocade shows a mix of matte ground and bright float.
surface.wear: Silk splits at the fold and the pleat; a gown is re-trimmed and re-cut for a new owner, so old pieces show many alterations.

palette.strategy: Pale ground colours with flower sprays in soft pink, blue and green; gold and silver thread for court.

processes: silk weaving on a Lyon draw loom
dressmaking by a marchande de modes and a couturière
pleating and draping on the body
embroidery and lace work by hand
making.scale: Made to order, one gown at a time, by a dressmaker and a trimmer; a court gown took many weeks.
making.signs: Hand-sewn pleats, pinned fronts, silk ruched by hand, and a lining that is cut separate from the gown.

emotion.target_response: A sense of play and rank: the viewer sees pale silk, lace and flowers, and reads wealth and ease.

use_cases: a period costume brief for a film about Louis XV or Louis XVI
a museum label for an 18th century gown
a fashion image prompt for a Rococo ball
avoid_when: the brief is plain or modern dress
the brief needs comfort and movement
the brief is a Regency or Empire dress

modifiers.how: Drop the hoops and the stays, lift the waist under the bust, and use white muslin.
Swap the cane hoops for a steel cage, round the skirt, and use a strong colour.

ornament_level.note: A day gown is lightly trimmed; a court gown carries lace and embroidery on every edge.
